A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same filler–gap intervention study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and support comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original intervention experiments, regressions, and cross-clausal transfer results in Sections 4–6, with additional model-size results in Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds PCA analyses of construction similarity in Section 5 and Appendix H.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same one-dimensional DAS intervention on Transformer-block outputs, with frozen language-model parameters and cross-entropy training of the intervention direction. The added PCA analyzes results rather than changing the intervention method.

E1.justification: Both use the same seven English filler–gap constructions, animate/inanimate extraction, single-/multi-clause variants, and English-EWT construction-frequency analysis. PCA introduces no additional data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The subject–verb agreement and transitive/intransitive lexical controls remain the evaluated comparators. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: v2 adds a per-position, two-component PCA procedure for analyzing generalization matrices in Section 5. Existing intervention settings remain unchanged, including the 400-sentence and 96-sentence evaluation sets already documented in v1 Appendix B.

E4.justification: v2 adds an exploratory analysis asking whether transfer profiles cluster by construction and animacy: Figure 5 covers Pythia-1.4b, and Appendix H Figure 20 covers 2.8b and 6.9b. The existing control, cross-clausal, and model-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain one-standard-error bars, Holm–Bonferroni-corrected t-tests, and the same mixed-effects regression significance reporting. v2 adds no seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty-estimation information.

E6.justification: v2 adds PCA clustering findings and changes Figure 4's plotted mean AUCs; for example, pseudocleft in-degree changes from approximately 0.51 to 0.40. The reason is unexplained, while the corresponding Appendix F panels, regression coefficients, and other matched result plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The DAS equation, graph-centrality/AUC definitions, and regression specifications retain their mathematical substance. No theorem, proof, or substantive formal derivation is added.

C1.justification: Both claim shared filler–gap mechanisms, modulation by linguistic similarity, animacy and frequency, and limited cross-clausal transfer. The expanded v2 introduction and conclusion emphasize findings already reported in v1, particularly Section 5.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges Transformer inductive biases as an unresolved alternative explanation for construction-dependent source strength in Section 8. It also adds a context-dependent mechanism interpretation in Section 6 and a concrete human-priming research direction in Section 7.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a repository address where v1 only promised a future code release. It also clarifies that NC positions are excluded from intervention training/testing and explains the evaluation-group mapping; training sample counts brought into the main text were already in v1 Appendix B.

R1.justification: v2 adds Rodriguez et al. (2025) as a related transfer-based study of semantic property inheritance and removes Portelance and Jasbi (2024). The broader research positioning is retained; publication updates to existing references do not introduce new works.

P1.justification: v2 expands the conclusion and experimental explanations, edits terminology and prose, and brings some appendix details into the main text. The overall section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds PCA Figures 5 and 20, merges v1's linguistic-feature Table 6 into Table 1, and moves v1's regression Table 8 into the main text as Table 2. Figure 4's axes and labels are revised, with additional caption edits and appendix rearrangement; most existing graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The added PCA check, clearer presentation of linguistic parameters and regression results, repository address, and explicit inductive-bias limitation modestly improve accessibility and transparency. These gains are partly offset by unexplained Figure 4 AUC revisions despite unchanged Appendix F panels. The core study and most evidence remain unchanged.
